```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
fig <- function(path) knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(path, mustWork=TRUE))
tab <- function(f,caption) knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path("report/audit",f)),digits=4,caption=caption)
```

This is an **AI-assisted reproducibility audit**, not the published supplement or a revised manuscript. It uses the corrected conservative commander lookup and R ordered logits described in `audit/README.md`. Read the [published paper](https://doi.org/10.3390/f11020169) separately. Missing original raw inputs prevent validating extraction; the missing complexity input prevents regenerating the map. Neither is substituted here. Archived figures/tables elsewhere in the repository remain reference outputs.

## Data and sample coverage

```{r}
tab("model-coverage.csv","Sample and fixed-effect counts by data path; legacy is a diagnostic with duplicate rows")
tab("commander_audit.csv","Conservative commander reconciliation: counts before order-model filtering")
tab("S1-summary.csv","S1: freshly computed numeric summaries of estimation samples")
```

Area/growth values use thousands of acres. `L1` denotes a one-period lag; current weather is `L0`. Growth-potential summaries use the ordered-logit sample; resource summaries use total-resource Model 1. Model-specific coverage appears above. The summaries do not establish equality of the samples' distributions.

## Outliers and principal components

```{r, out.width='80%'}
fig(c("report/audit/figures/outliers.png","report/audit/figures/PCA.png"))
```

The PCA and outlier rules retain the source workflow. This audit does not validate raw database extraction or revisit the substantive choice of those rules.

## Fire growth: Table S2 and Figure 3 panels

Quasipoisson models retain the original formulas. Standard errors cluster on fire.

```{r}
tab("S2-growth.csv","S2: all fitted terms with fire-clustered SEs")
```

```{r, out.width='48%'}
fig(file.path("report/audit/figures",paste0(c("prcp","rmin","tmax","wind","bi","erc","sfwp"),".png")))
```

## Growth potential: Table S3 and Figure 4

These are R cumulative-logit maximum-likelihood fits with fire-clustered covariance. They use Low/Medium/High/Extreme outcomes and the source do-file's Low terrain reference, GACC/year/cause indicators, seasonal interactions, PCs and restricted-cubic area spline. Saved Stata coefficients do not all match at printed precision. The comparison file reports discrepancies without relaxing the threshold.

```{r}
tab("gp-coefficients.csv","S3: R ordered-logit coefficients, thresholds and fire-clustered SEs")
```

```{r, out.width='95%'}
fig("report/audit/figures/Figure4_R.png")
```

```{r, out.width='48%'}
fig(file.path("report/audit/figures",paste0("gp_",c("prcp","tmax","wind","bi","sfwp"),"_R.png")))
```

Curves average counterfactual probabilities over the estimation sample. Bars are normal delta-method 95% intervals using fire-clustered covariance, not predictions at mean covariates.

## Resource orders: main Tables 3–6 and S4–S5

Labels map by term name, so `L1.growth` is **Lagged Growth** and `evac_potential` is **Potential Evacuation**. Unlike the old renderer, these outputs explicitly request fire-clustered standard errors. Fixed-effect counts come from fitted models. The High-growth coefficient is conditional on no potential evacuation in models containing that interaction; it is not an unconditional average effect.

```{r}
tab("Table3.csv","Table 3: corrected resource-order sample")
tab("Table4.csv","Table 4: total resource orders")
tab("Table5.csv","Table 5: engines and crews")
tab("Table6.csv","Table 6: aircraft, helicopters and dozers")
x<-read.csv("report/audit/resource-coefficients-all-paths.csv")
knitr::kable(x[x$variant=="corrected",],digits=4,caption="S4–S5: all resource-order terms; corrected path")
```

These are conditional observational associations. The audit does not identify a causal response to perceived risk, evacuation potential or weather. Before/after estimates and significance changes are summarized in `audit/RESULTS.md`.
